overview: Immunity can be acquired either through everyday natural exposure or through deliberate medical intervention.
genZNote: Natural immunity: your body handling things on its own. Artificial immunity: medicine giving your body a helping hand.

aspects.label: How It's Acquired
aspects.valueA: Acquired through natural exposure to a pathogen (infection) or transfer of antibodies (like mother to baby).
aspects.valueB: Acquired through deliberate medical intervention such as vaccination or antiserum injection.

aspects.label: Example (Active Form)
aspects.valueA: Recovering from a chickenpox infection, gaining lifelong immunity.
aspects.valueB: Getting a measles vaccine to trigger the same lifelong immunity artificially.

aspects.label: Example (Passive Form)
aspects.valueA: A baby receiving antibodies through the placenta or breast milk.
aspects.valueB: Receiving anti-venom or antiserum after a snakebite.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Both natural and artificial immunity can further be split into active (body makes its own antibodies) and passive (antibodies given ready-made).
overlay.memoryTrick: Natural = life gives it to you. Artificial = medicine gives it to you.
overlay.commonMisconception: Artificial immunity isn't 'fake' or weaker — a vaccine (artificial active immunity) can provide just as strong and lasting protection as a natural infection, often more safely.
